caption:
You know the email. Client's invoice is 15 days overdue, and you're staring at a blank reply trying to sound firm without sounding rude.

As of August 18, Claude can actually send that email for you — not just draft it. Connect Gmail, give it the invoice details, and it prepares the message. You still click approve before anything goes out.

The prompt on slide 4 is what to paste once you've connected Gmail. Save this so you're not rewriting the same overdue-payment email every month.

Follow @leverageai.daily — one AI workflow a day for people who run their own business.

body.t: Since August 18, Claude can send, reply to, and forward email — not just draft it. Turn on the Gmail connector in
Every send goes through a confirm step: Claude prepares the email, you read it, you click send.
Nothing leaves your inbox without your say-so
— unless you turn that off. Don't, for money emails.

slides.headline: Queue the follow-up.
slides.sub: Paste this once Claude can see your invoice details.
slides.label: COPY THIS PROMPT
slides.code:
Client: [name]
Invoice #: [number], due [date]
Days overdue: [X]
Write a short, firm-but-friendly email
asking for payment. No apology, no
guilt. End with a clear next step.
Prepare it to send from my Gmail —
wait for my approval first.

body.t: Write actions are confirmed for Gmail; if you're on Outlook or another provider,
check before you rely on it
. And approval-off is a real setting — leave it on for anything involving money.
